metadata.subtitle: The Client-Report Skill (Anthropic Skills)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: take the client-report skill apart. Is it a built-in finance app with hidden logic, or a plain-text file Claude reads and executes? Explain the actual mechanism — SKILL.md as instruction set, Steps as a linear pipeline — then name the design trade-off: full repeatability inside the spec, model judgment outside it. The carry-out lands that the file's coverage is what repeats; whatever it doesn't say, Claude works out on its own.

beats.narration_text: Here's the wrong guess — that Claude's client-report is a built-in finance app, tuned for the task with hidden logic underneath. It isn't. It's a plain-text skill Claude reads before it works. So the real question: does it understand finance, or is it just following steps?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 1.0 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('app' -> 'skill') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends. Text/rates chosen from the established hai-simple fix pattern (42ms/char, 4% mistakeRate, 8% hesitateBetween, 4-line/64-char text) after the agent-development sibling's first-attempt timeout at slower/higher rates.

beats.narration_text: Here's what a skill actually is: a folder Claude reads before it works. Client-report has one SKILL.md file inside — the full instruction set, plain English, no hidden code. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The pipeline lives in one section of the file — Steps. Claude reads it, runs each step in order, returns the result. Linear on purpose: no branching unless a step itself asks for one.

Here's what client-report's SKILL.md actually spells out: portfolio returns, an allocation breakdown, market commentary, timed for quarterly or annual delivery. Inside that scope, feed the same numbers twice and it builds the same report twice. Step outside — a chart type the file never mentions, a client segment it doesn't list — and there's no instruction to fall back on. Claude reasons past the file on its own. The trade-off is honest: full repeatability inside the spec, model judgment outside it.

beats.narration_text: A Claude skill isn't a hidden app — it's a plain-text file of instructions, so the same input produces the same report every time. Whatever that file doesn't say, Claude has to work out on its own.

props.quote: A Claude skill isn't a hidden app — it's a plain-text file of instructions, so the same input produces the same report every time. Whatever that file doesn't say, Claude has to work out on its own.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt — paste it into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Pick a recurring report you know well: a weekly team update, a monthly client summary, a project status. Write me a SKILL.md for it. Include, one, the full instruction set in plain English, as numbered Steps Claude follows in order; two, an explicit In-Scope list — every item the file specifies; three, an explicit Out-of-Scope list — every decision the file leaves for Claude to reason past on its own. Go deeper: for a report you actually depend on, which items on that Out-of-Scope list would you regret leaving to Claude's judgment — and how would you rewrite the SKILL.md to move them into the file? Liam, in for Bear.
